full_judgment:
3. The defendant's case is that plot No. 1292 which is the disputed plot including. plot of 1291 and 1304 of Khatian 65 belonged to Jalauddin and others in korfa under the jote recorded in khatian No. 63 in the name of Kalimuddin Shaikh. The Babus purchased the jote of khatian No. 65 but the said was subsequently purchased in auction by one Baru Bibi. It was the further case of the defendants that Baru Bibi after having gone into khas possession of the same sold it to one Saila Bala by registered kabala dated 11-8-38 and the said Saila Bala thereafter leased out to defendant no. 1 by a registered kabuliyat (Ext. C) dated 19-3-40 1'52 acres of plot no. 1290,1291 and 1261 and they had been in possession of the same by erecting Basa Bari on plot no. 1292. The further case of the defendant that the aforesaid lease was taken in the banami of his minor son and that he never leased out to the plaintiff at any point of time the plot bing no. 1292 and there was no talk of leasing out the same at the time of the patta dated 28-2-1945 and there was no fraudulent insertion also in the said Kabuliyat as alleged. The defendant's further case is that the plaintiff forcibly entered into his homestead in plot no. 1292 and erected huts there and are in possession thereof. The land has been rightly recorded in his name and the plaintiff has no case. 

 6. Mr. Syed Shamsur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents of the other hand has argued that the judgment and decree as passed by the learned Additional District Judge need not be interfered by this Court in appeal because the court in arriving at the finding that there was nothing to prove any fraud on record or mistaken description of the property inadvertently by the parties concerned it can not be said to be finding falling under proviso (1) to Section 92 of the Evidence Act and that being so plots described in a registered document being the terms of the contract cannot be varied by oral evidence between the parties and the document need be read as it is found written, expressing the intention of the  parties in executing the document. He further submits that there was no question of fraud or mistake in the case as the document clearly recited the plots to be plot nos. 1290, 1291 total area being 2'46, under khatian no 65. (and that being so plot no. 1292 covering an area of 2'86 each is more than the area of 2'46 as in the disputed kabuliyat cannot be read into because in that case it will change not only the plot numbers but also the area of the land leased out and there cannot be mistake on both the counts and thus he submits that the court of the learned Additional District Judge was correct in holding that the plaintiff is not entitled to the relief sought for. Mr. Rahman, the Advocate argued also on the point of limitation.
